rejected.title: The Constitution of 1787
card: The Articles of Confederation left the national government weak. In 1787, delegates met in Philadelphia and wrote a new constitution to replace them.
Federalism
power is shared between a national government and the state governments. The national government gained powers the Articles had denied it, such as taxing.
Separation of powers
the framers feared any one group holding all power, so they split it among three branches. Congress makes laws, the president carries them out, and the courts judge disputes under the law.
Checks and balances
each branch can limit the others. For example, the president can veto a law passed by Congress, and the Senate must approve top officials.
rejected.remember: The Constitution shared power between nation and states, and split and checked power inside the national government.

a.q: Why did the Constitution divide power among three branches?
opts: So that no single group could hold all national power
So that the states could no longer have any powers
So that the national government could stay weak
So that the president could make laws without Congress
a.why: The framers feared any one group holding all power, so they split it among Congress, the president and the courts. The states kept some powers, so the aim was not to remove them, and the new government gained powers such as taxing, so it was not meant to stay weak.
a.clue: Think about what the framers feared if one group held all power.

b.q: Congress passes a law and the president vetoes it. Which feature of the Constitution does this show?
opts: Checks and balances, as one branch limits another
Federalism, as the states limit the national government
Separation of powers only, as the branches never overlap
The Articles of Confederation, as Congress had no power
b.why: The president is using a power to limit what Congress has done, which is a check by one branch on another. It is not federalism, because no state government is involved in the veto.
b.clue: Which two parts of government are pulling against each other?

opts: So that no single group could hold all national power
So that the states could no longer have any powers
So that the national government could stay weak
So that the president could make laws without Congress
a.why: Splitting power among Congress, the president and the courts meant no one group could control everything. The states kept some powers, so the idea was not to remove them, and the aim was a government that could act, not a weak one.

The Articles of Confederation, as Congress had no power
